page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Marginal notes stand in the left margin (three) and the right margin (about three). Running head at top right, page number at top left. No catchword.

main_text.p: præcipitijs. Artibus excúlti, gradibus ornati, lucí mundi expósiti, quid facimus, aut quas gratias Deo rependimus? Homo in honore non intelligit, sed similis est jumentis, quæ intereunt. PC.49.[?] Nisi igitur inter nonnullos Lurcones, Turbones, Bibones, Dominus exercituum reliquisset nobis aliquod Ingeniorum semen, quasi Sodoma fuissemus (ut loquitur de suis Prophetæ) aut Gomorrhæ similes. Isai.1.[?]

7 Sed nimius fortasse fui in urendo & se-cando; Regredior ad vos (Baccalaurei) mei malleo pro tempore incudes. Cogitate vos hodie saltum[?] nelle[?] fluentem ingredi: Affectibus proculdubio vestris, pro ætate ductilioribus in posterum ingerentur, carnis, Mundi & Diaboli, mellita, sed lethalia incantamenta. Torrentes Belial, Baal[?], Satanæ, ut Tormenta totidem bellica, in vestram obsidionem erunt ex-positæ. 1.Pet.5.[?] Tendiculas struet Tartarius iste Sophista in cibo vestro, & potu, & graduum privi-legijs, ut nova dignitas aut scientia inflet, aut amoto custode, aut collato libertatis pileo abducat licentia. Venenum instillabit otio, liberta-ti, & Mæcenatum, quibus fruimur; beneficijs, ut morositas vel socordia nos dementet. Studia nostra

page.notes: Left-margin notes are short references, read with doubt: the first at the level of "intelligit" (possibly "Psal. 49."), the second at "Prophetæ" (possibly "Isai. 1."). A small illegible mark sits in the left margin beside "lucí mundi" and another in the right margin near "pileo"; both are unreadable. Right-margin note at "Tormenta" is a reference, read as "1.Pet.5." with doubt. Greek word after "Torrentes Belial," is printed in Greek letters and could not be read reliably; "Baal[?]" is a best guess. "saltum" and "nelle" are doubtful. A small mark "4" with a flourish sits below the last line at the bottom left; it is not clearly printed text and was not transcribed. Italic and roman distinctions are approximate. Printed hyphens at line ends (privi-legijs, liberta-ti, se-cando, ex-positæ) are kept as printed. Spelling "vrendo" is given as "urendo" under the u/v rule.
